children: SYDNEY--Kimberly-Clark's US$40 billion acquisition of Kenvue has been approved by Australia's competition regulator on condition that the group divests of two local period-care brands.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission said Wednesday that Kimberly-Clark must sell Kenvue's Carefree and Stayfree brands to an approved buyer to avoid triggering regulatory concerns over market concentration and consumer choice.
Without the divestments, Kimberly-Clark's acquisition of Kenvue would have reduced the number of major period-care suppliers in Australia from three to two, the ACCC said.

"The divestiture will preserve an independent competitor in the supply of period-care products in Australia and maintain the competition that would otherwise be lost," ACCC Commissioner Philip Williams said.
Kimberly-Clark proposed the divestment to the ACCC in July.
